The REST module reaches `OrderService.getOrderTypes` from three production call sites in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, plus several test call sites. The core platform defines the method in `openmrs-core`, where the service interface, implementation, DAO and Hibernate DAO all declare it.

**Production callers in the core REST module (`/ws/rest/v1`):**

1. **`OrderTypeResource1_10.doGetAll`** (line 122) returns all order types, so a change in behaviour or ordering reaches `GET /ws/rest/v1/ordertype` listings directly. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_10/OrderTypeResource1_10.java:120-123`
2. **`OrderTypeResource1_10.doSearch`** (line 130) fetches all order types and filters them by the `q` name pattern, so search results are affected too. Same file, `:128-139`
3. **`OrderableResource1_10.search`** (line 69) calls `getOrderTypes(false)` and passes the result to `getOrderableConceptClasses`, which derives the orderable concept classes. This affects the orderable search endpoint. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_10/OrderableResource1_10.java:65-70` (the method continues past line 79; I did not read to its end)

**Test call sites** (these would fail or need updating if the behaviour changed):

4. `OrderTypeController1_10Test` uses `getOrderTypes(false)` and `getOrderTypes(true)` at lines 55, 99, 147 and 157, in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_10/OrderTypeController1_10Test.java`.

**Core definitions** (the behaviour under change):

- `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/OrderServiceImpl.java:1002`
- `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/OrderService.java:811`
- `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/hibernate/HibernateOrderDAO.java:750`
- `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/OrderDAO.java:200`

Falkon's `find_symbol_references` and a repo-wide grep returned the same seven call sites, so I'm fairly confident the REST module has no other direct callers. I did not check the `openmrs-module-webservices.rest` 2.x resources or other modules that might reach the service indirectly.
